questions.question: Why do alkanes resist most reagents while alkenes react readily?
questions.solution: Alkanes hold only strong, non-polar σ bonds with no electron-rich region to attack — no 'handle' for electrophiles or nucleophiles. Alkenes expose a π bond: electron-dense and loosely held, it attracts electrophiles and can open without breaking the σ framework. Reactivity follows available electron density.

questions.question: HBr adds to propene giving 2-bromopropane. Justify the regiochemistry through the intermediate.
questions.solution: Protonation can give a 1° or a 2° carbocation; the 2° (more hyperconjugation, more +I stabilisation) forms preferentially, and Br⁻ then attacks it — placing Br on the middle carbon. Markovnikov's rule is a CONSEQUENCE of carbocation stability, not an arbitrary rule.

questions.question: Why does bromine water lose its colour with an alkene but not with an alkane? What does the observation certify?
questions.solution: The alkene's π bond attacks Br₂, adding across the double bond (forming a dibromide) and consuming the bromine — the red-brown colour disappears instantly. An alkane has no π bond; substitution under these conditions is negligible, so colour persists. Rapid decolourisation of Br₂ water is the standard unsaturation test.

questions.question: Why does benzene resist addition reactions that alkenes undergo readily?
questions.solution: Addition would destroy the delocalised π system (aromaticity) — benzene's resonance stabilisation (~150 kJ/mol) would be lost. Substitution keeps the aromatic ring intact: one group replaces another and the stabilised system survives. Benzene pays the activation cost to AVOID losing aromaticity.

questions.question: Why are fused-ring aromatics like benzo[a]pyrene carcinogenic?
questions.solution: Their flat, extended π systems intercalate between DNA base pairs; metabolic oxidation converts them to reactive epoxides that bind covalently to DNA, causing mutations. Planarity (intercalation) plus metabolic activation is the structure–hazard link.
